courses.name: Personal & Professional Development
courses.contribution: Mandatory Year-1 development.

courses.name: Accounting & Corporate Finance
courses.contribution: Direct accounting contribution: accepted accounting theory and practice, corporate annual reports and financial-statement analysis support organisational decisions. The title alone does not establish the whole external corporate-finance syllabus.

courses.name: Business & Economy in the Age of AI
courses.contribution: examines managerial, organisational and societal implications of AI and technological change

courses.name: Transnational Business Law
courses.contribution: covers legal frameworks for contracts, trade, company activity and digital commerce across borders

courses.name: Money, Banking & Finance
courses.contribution: Direct financial decision-making: cases develop analysis of financial data, risk, investment, budgeting and business value. This is partial corporate-finance correspondence, not identical external coverage.

courses.name: Introduction to Economics
courses.contribution: provides economic foundations on firms, markets, incentives and macroeconomic conditions

courses.name: International Macroeconomics
courses.contribution: examines growth, inflation, business cycles and policy shaping the international business environment

courses.name: Microeconomics & Behavior
courses.contribution: develops microeconomic and behavioural analysis of consumer and firm decisions

courses.name: Public Economics
courses.contribution: examines market failure, externalities, taxation and public intervention affecting firms

courses.name: Econometrics
courses.contribution: provides econometric tools for causal and predictive analysis of business data

courses.name: Consumer Product Design
courses.contribution: develops product innovation through customer needs, design, costing and team development

courses.name: Marketing & Consumer Engagement
courses.contribution: examines marketing strategy, consumer psychology and responsible customer engagement

courses.name: Strategy & Digital Transformation
courses.contribution: develops business strategy from vision to execution and responsible digital transformation

courses.name: Market Research
courses.contribution: Direct applied empirical business research: students plan and conduct real market research, analyse results and formulate business recommendations. This course-based project does not reproduce a separate 12-EC bachelor thesis.

courses.name: International Business & Governance
courses.contribution: examines institutions, culture, governance and corporate responsibility in global business

courses.name: Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations
courses.contribution: provides business foundations while developing venture creation, business models and market validation

courses.name: Research Methods & Statistics
courses.contribution: provides research design, surveys, experiments and statistical analysis for management questions

courses.name: Personal Leadership
courses.contribution: develops leadership theory, self-awareness and applied leadership practice

courses.name: Leadership Communication
courses.contribution: develops leadership communication, ethical influence and persuasive practice

courses.name: Leadership & Diversity Management
courses.contribution: examines inclusive leadership and diversity management in organisations

courses.name: Psychology of Organizations & Leadership
courses.contribution: examines motivation, groups, organisational culture and structures through organisational psychology

courses.name: Negotiation & Strategic Thinking
courses.contribution: Direct business negotiation and influence: persuasive arguments, language, negotiation processes and interest-based strategic interaction. This is not a general corporate-strategy counterpart.

courses.name: AI Ethics
courses.contribution: examines ethical and societal questions raised by artificial intelligence

courses.name: Database Management Systems
courses.contribution: Complementary analytical tools: provides relational database and SQL skills for structured data. Application to business is supplied by the programme, not guaranteed in this course.

courses.name: Algorithms & Data Structures
courses.contribution: Complementary analytical tools: develops algorithmic problem-solving and data structures for computational applications. Application to business is supplied by the programme, not guaranteed in this course.

courses.name: Introduction to Data Science
courses.contribution: Complementary analytical tools: develops data cleaning, visualisation and manipulation across disciplinary datasets. Application to business is supplied by the programme, not guaranteed in this course.

courses.name: Machine Learning
courses.contribution: introduces machine-learning models for prediction and analysis of real datasets

courses.name: Neural Networks & Deep Learning
courses.contribution: Complementary analytical tools: develops neural-network and deep-learning methods for advanced AI applications. Application to business is supplied by the programme, not guaranteed in this course.

courses.name: Introduction to Programming
courses.contribution: Complementary analytical tools: provides programming foundations in Python. Application to business is supplied by the programme, not guaranteed in this course.

courses.name: Mathematical Methods
courses.contribution: Complementary analytical tools: provides mathematical foundations for quantitative modelling. Application to business is supplied by the programme, not guaranteed in this course.

courses.name: Linear Algebra
courses.contribution: Complementary analytical tools: provides linear-algebra foundations for quantitative and machine-learning models. Application to business is supplied by the programme, not guaranteed in this course.

courses.name: Probability & Statistics
courses.contribution: Complementary analytical tools: provides probability, statistical inference and simulation foundations for risk and analytics. Application to business is supplied by the programme, not guaranteed in this course.

courses.name: R3: Recycling, Recovery, Remediation
courses.contribution: Environmental science/technical or sector-specific content has insufficient business-management weight here; replaced by stronger business or empirical-method content.

courses.name: Governance of Sustainability
courses.contribution: Complementary regulatory and societal context: governmental and nongovernmental actors, interests, public opinion and policy enforcement explain sustainability governance. This is not a dedicated responsible-organisation course.

courses.name: Sustainable Farming & Innovation
courses.contribution: Environmental science/technical or sector-specific content has insufficient business-management weight here; replaced by stronger business or empirical-method content.

courses.name: Sustainability Essentials I
courses.contribution: Complementary environmental framework: planetary boundaries identify environmental limits relevant to responsible products and business strategy; this is not business management training.

courses.name: Sustainability Essentials II
courses.contribution: Environmental science/technical or sector-specific content has insufficient business-management weight here; replaced by stronger business or empirical-method content.

courses.name: Climate Change
courses.contribution: Complementary climate context: anthropogenic drivers, environmental and societal impacts, adaptation, mitigation, climate governance and justice inform sustainable business risk and responsibility.

courses.name: Life Cycle Analysis & Circular Economy
courses.contribution: Direct sustainable product and process analysis: life-cycle environmental evaluation and strategic circular-economy planning support responsible enterprise decisions.

courses.name: Renewable System Design
courses.contribution: Environmental science/technical or sector-specific content has insufficient business-management weight here; replaced by stronger business or empirical-method content.

courses.name: Ethics
courses.contribution: Complementary normative reasoning: virtue ethics, deontology and utilitarianism, responsibility, equality, wealth, future generations and climate support ethical business judgments. No dedicated business-ethics case syllabus is claimed.

courses.name: Qualitative Research Methodology
courses.contribution: Complementary empirical method: qualitative question design, interpretation, small-team projects and reflexivity about complexity and power support organisational inquiry; business topics are not guaranteed.

courses.name: Social Psychology
courses.contribution: Complementary behavioural foundations: scientific social psychology examines how others influence thought, feelings and behaviour; its organisational or customer application is specific supporting work.

courses.name: The Art of Rhetorical Communication
courses.contribution: Complementary academic and professional communication: rhetorical analysis, argument, academic writing and oral presentation support communicating organisational research. Historical and contemporary rhetoric is not an empirical business-research course.
